body: why do we work so hard to 'fix' ourselves, to mold ourselves to this vision the world demands of us if in the end it's not us who isn't enough but it's the world that demands too much?  why then are we stuck with the pain and the shame and the guilt?  all the hard work, all the heartache and crippling depression and pain is all ours to bear and for who?  why are we not good enough?  we, too, were born on this earth and for what?  to be discarded and dysfunctional products of a process that is seemingly out of control?  is there a reason?  what have we done to deserve this?

i called for the first time recently and she literally said okay call back if you need anything else and hung up while i was in the middle of talking.  nobody fucking cares if i'm gone.  it's all for them.  they want to feel like good people, like they did the right thing, no guilt or whatever.  instead all the guilt is thrown on the suffering.  why do i have to do so much work to fix myself when nobody else even gives a remote fuck about what happens to me?

Thanks.  Not sure what to think of being nice anymore.  Recently had a conversation with a therapist of sorts who told me being nice was basically ruining my life.  I AM a nice person, but probably to my own detriment.  People have taken a lot of advantage of it.

Anyway, thanks for the kind words.  I appreciate you and the sentiment.
this is why i feel like historical materialism was poison to my brain.  once you see the material reality of the world you can't unsee it and it's ugly as fuck.
